sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Cosmetics and Personal Care Products

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (national-level unitary incorporation; RCS registration with the relevant tribunal de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 30 May 1984, entered into force 28 March 1985, as amended by Protocol of 30 November 2007)
France–China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 30 November 1984; most recently amended by Protocol of 28 November 2013)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (political agreement reached 30 December 2020; ratification pending)
France–United States Tax Convention (1994) as amended by the Protocols of 2006 and 2009
EU–Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (provisionally applied since 21 September 2017)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II — Articles L. 210-1 et seq. on general incorporation rules, L. 227-1 to L. 227-19 on the Société par Actions Simplifiée, and R. 123-31 et seq. on registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's territorial jurisdiction, through the INPI Guichet Unique des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de création d'entreprise (M0 formalities dossier) submitted electronically via the Guichet Unique; registration is evidenced by the Extrait Kbis.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the articles of association freely fix the capital. Cash contributions must be deposited and blocked in a regulated French bank until registration, and at least 50% of cash contribution value must be paid up at subscription, with the balance payable within five years.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial share capital set forth in the statuts is subscribed in full by the founding shareholders and that cash contributions shall be deposited at a regulated French bank and remain blocked until registration, in accordance with the Code de commerce. RESOLVED, that the registered office is hereby fixed at the address in the statuts and that all statutory notices, filings, and correspondence shall be directed there. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Président of the Société par Actions Simplifiée for an indefinite term, with full powers to manage and bind the Company, and that [Name] is appointed legal representative for registrations before the RCS and all public authorities. All founding actions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and signing of the corporate articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders / notary public (optional for authentic statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French in accordance with the Code de commerce, including corporate name, purpose, registered office, duration, capital, classes of shares, president's powers, and shareholder decision rules. Have all shareholders sign, or use a notarial act when in-kind real property contributions are made. Obtain the appointed president's consent and non-condemnation declaration.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (electronic or original)
Valid identity documents of all shareholders
Justificatif de domiciliation (proof of registered office address or domiciliation contract)
Attestation de non-condamnation of the appointed president
Consent to appointment from the president and legal representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry notes omissions, amend the statuts by a supplementary act before filing; material changes require re-execution by all shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital account and deposit of cash contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A regulated bank established in France or la Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For cash contributions, open a provisional blocked account in the company's name and deposit the required funds before filing. Request an attestation de dépôt des fonds / attestation de blocage for the registry. Funds may be released only after the Extrait Kbis is issued and the legal representative is identified.
required_dossiers: Project statuts
Bank corporate onboarding and KYC documents
Identity documents of authorized signatories
Instruction letter specifying the blocked nature and amount of the deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses opening, use another regulated French financial institution; the attestation must be issued by the institution actually holding the blocked funds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the mandatory legal notice in an approved announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a formal notice containing the corporate name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, president's identity, and the RCS city. Submit the notice to an approved JAL and obtain the attestation de parution, which must be included in the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Text of legal notice
Project or executed statuts
Identity details of the president and shareholders, if requested by the journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is incomplete, publish a corrective notice in the same or another approved JAL and obtain a new attestation before proceeding with the main filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing with the Guichet Unique des Entreprises (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), routed to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online creation dossier for a Société par Actions Simplifiée, upload all required dossiers, and pay the official registration fee. The dossier is automatically transmitted to the competent registry, which checks legal conformity. Upon acceptance the company is registered in the RCS and an Extrait Kbis is issued.
required_dossiers: M0 online creation data / standard formation form
Signed statuts
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (bank blocking certificate)
Attestation de parution in a journal d'annonces légales
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs (declaration of beneficial owners)
Attestation de non-condamnation of legal representatives
Proof of registered office / domiciliation contract
Identity documents of shareholders and legal representatives
Payment receipt of official filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an incompleteness or objection notice, correct and resubmit the dossier through the Guichet Unique within the indicated deadline. In case of refusal or silence, petition the juge du registre at the competent tribunal de commerce for an order to proceed with registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration issuance of identifying numbers and administrative activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE (Sirene), Direction Générale des Finances Publiques, and URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, retrieve the Kbis. INSEE automatically assigns the SIRET and APE/NAF code; the tax administration assigns the intra-Community VAT number where the company is subject to VAT. Verify all identifiers on the Kbis and complete any sectoral declarations required for cosmetics retail, such as product notifications via the CPNP when placing finished cosmetic products on the market.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
RCS registration number
APE/NAF code assigned by INSEE
Tax identification and VAT documentation
Social security registration confirmation from URSSAF
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an identification number is missing or incorrect, file a rectification request with the Greffe for RCS/Kbis data or with INSEE Sirene for SIRET/APE data; tax and social identifiers may be corrected through impots.gouv.fr and the relevant URSSAF office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to pure online retail of cosmetics; for any ancillary physical store or warehouse, the local urban planning and commercial licensing authorities (e.g., commission départementale d'aménagement commercial) and DREETS would exercise jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating or manufacturing license is required for distance selling of cosmetics under French law; product compliance under Regulation (EC) No 1223/2009 and CPNP notification are product-safety obligations, not establishment licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) / Ministère de la Transition Écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — pure e-commerce retail is not within the environmental impact assessment categories of Annexe à l'article R. 122-2 du Code de l'environnement and does not trigger an installation classée pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial VOC or wastewater discharge thresholds are triggered by online-only retail; sanitary wastewater must comply with applicable municipal discharge limits under the Code de la Santé publique, and packaging waste extended producer responsibility obligations under the Code de l'environnement (AGEC law) must be fulfilled through certified eco-organizations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil defense or fire-safety certificate is required for an online-only head office. If the company opens a warehouse or customer-facing store, it must obtain fire safety inspection and approval from the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours, structural and electrical conformity certification, and DREETS occupational health and safety clearance before operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), operating via impots.gouv.fr; entity registration executed through the Guichet Unique and the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE); VAT and corporate tax administration by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); non-established foreign sellers register with the DGFiP's dedicated non-resident unit (SIE Non-Résidents).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SAS through the Guichet Unique to obtain the 9-digit SIREN (national identifier) and SIRET (establishment identifier) allocated by INSEE. Step 2: DGFiP automatically assigns a TVA intracommunautaire registration number (FR + 2-digit control key + SIREN) upon commencement of taxable activity; the number is activated for intra-Community declarations via the EORI-linked VAT dashboard. Step 3: For foreign non-established entities: file the specific VAT registration application with DGFiP (non-resident procedure), and if established outside the EEA, appoint a tax representative (représentant fiscal) jointly liable for VAT under Article 289 A CGI. Step 4: For online and cross-border distance sales, register with the French OSS (One Stop Shop) for intra-EU sales or IOSS for imports of low-value consignments not exceeding EUR 150. Step 5: Apply for an EORI number (FR + SIREN) for customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, or IS) at entity level. Option for a passthrough-like income tax regime (Impôt sur le Revenu, or IR) is available under Article 239 bis A / 239 bis AA CGI: small, newly created SAS (less than 5 years old, fewer than 50 employees, annual turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, and at least 75% of capital held by natural persons) may elect IR taxation for the first 5 fiscal years; election must be transmitted to the SIE by the filing deadline of the first return. VAT election: French franchise en base de TVA (VAT registration threshold EUR 85,000 for goods) cannot be used for online marketplace-facilitated sales or by non-established sellers, but a resident SAS may apply it for small direct retail turnover. IT/export-related treaties and hybrid mismatch: France applies Article 212 bis CGI implementing ATAD; no elective hybrid-check-the-box mechanism exists in France and artificial hybrid structures are disregarded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.territorial_overlay_note: France applies unitary national taxation; no state-level corporate tax or sub-national VAT; local territorial economic contribution (CFE/CVAE) applies at municipal/departmental level but is outside the VAT/corporate income tax identity framework.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic established taxpayers: EUR 85,000 annual turnover for goods (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B CGI) before mandatory registration; for services the threshold is EUR 37,500. Non-established foreign entities: zero threshold; VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction in France. For e-commerce distance selling of cosmetics to French consumers: the EU cross-border threshold of EUR 10,000 (intra-EU distance sales) applies for OSS; sales above the threshold are taxable in France at 20%. Online marketplace rules under Article 283 CGI may deem the marketplace operator to be the supplier when it facilitates delivery through its platform (dropshipping); Shopify/PayPal as payment rails do not in themselves create the nexus, nexus is founded on the French establishment/warehouse and place-of-supply of B2C goods under Article 258 CGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has adopted mandatory electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) phased under the Loi de finances 2024: from 1 September 2026, all VAT-registered businesses must be able to receive e-invoices, and large enterprises and mid-caps must issue e-invoices through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Partenaire de Dématérialisation (PDP); from 1 September 2027, small and mid-sized businesses (including typical SAS retail entities) must issue e-invoices equally. B2B invoices must use structured electronic formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII) with XML and mandatory electronic signature (Cachet); the PDP/PPF performs interoperability checks, and transaction data reaches DGFiP through e-reporting via API (no classical real-time tax clearance counter, but non-compliant invoices are rejected). Penalties escalate from EUR 15 per non-compliant invoice up to EUR 15,000 per entity per month for systematic non-transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cosmetics (HS 3304/3305/3307) physically exported from France to a destination outside the European Union are zero-rated under Article 262-I CGI, provided title transfer occurred in France or the EU and the goods leave the EU customs territory within 90 days from the date of the relevant invoice (demonstrated by the export customs declaration). Intra-EU dispatches to VAT-registered businesses are exempt under Article 262 ter CGI subject to the buyer's valid TVA intracommunautaire number and the EC Sales List/DEB being filed. B2C distance sales to EU consumers are not zero-rated; they fall under OSS/IOSS and are taxable in the destination member state. Offshore services (e.g., formulation services, IT support, brand licensing for non-EU customers) may be zero-rated under Articles 259 and 259 A-D CGI where the recipient is established outside the EU and the benefit is located abroad; the invoice must state the reason for zero-rating (0% TVA - exportation / services hors UE).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU / DES H1 declaration) lodged in the DELTA-X customs system and the customs clearance receipt with the 10-digit export code
Commercial Invoice describing the cosmetics (US/HTS/HS codes 3304/3305/3307) and stating the Incoterms and export zero-rating clause
Bill of Lading (Connaissement maritime) or Air Waybill (LTA) evidencing the physical exit of goods from the EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Attestation de Change) or bank SWIFT/MT103 statement evidencing payment received in EUR from a non-French and non-EU account

CN 22/CN 23 customs declaration (for postal/parcel consignments) and, where applicable, the Proof of Export (AEP) or ECS documentation; for intra-EU dispatches, the buyer's TVA intracommunautaire number and the EC Sales List (Déclaration d'Échange de Biens - DEB)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are systematically verified by DGFiP through physical-goods-exit audits, reconciliation with customs data (DELTA-X), and review of the Attestation de Change. Failure to substantiate physical export within 90 days triggers retrospective recharacterization as domestic supply: VAT at 20% is clawed back from the original invoice date with statutory late-payment interest (intérêt de retard of 0.20% per month under Article 1727 CGI). Penalties for fraud include: 40% increase for bad-faith inaccuracies (Article 1729(a) CGI), 80% increase for fraudulent maneuvers (Article 1729(b) CGI), and criminal sanctions of EUR 500,000 fine and 5 years imprisonment for tax fraud under Article 1741 CGI, plus publication of the sanction and referral to the Commission des Infractions Fiscales; refunds may be suspended and an audit of prior six-year limb can be reopened under Article L. 169 Livre des Procédures Fiscales.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), together with the ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) for banking licensing/AML supervision, and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for external financial policy. The European Central Bank (ECB) is the ultimate monetary authority for euro issuance and stability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account transactions (goods, services, income) and capital-account operations (investment, loans, dividends) in France, as guaranteed by Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Code Monétaire et Financier. For a French SAS, profit remittance (dividends, shareholder loan repayments, royalties) to EU/EEA investors is unrestricted; remittance to non-EU parties may require standard tax forms (e.g., Form 2766-SD for earnings distributed to non-residents) and must comply with EU sanctions and anti-money-laundering reporting, but no foreign-exchange approval or conversion quota is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists in French law. French exporters may freely invoice in any currency, retain foreign-currency balances, and convert them at their Bank of France-regulated financial institution without repatriation deadlines. However, the SAS must report all cross-border payment flows to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics when current thresholds are met (typically EUR 15,000 per transaction for the general monthly reporting), and the company must annually declare any foreign bank accounts on the French tax return (Article 1649 A CGI).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE SA (Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Épargne networks)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for a standard-risk e-commerce operator using EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Treezor, or passported EU EMIs like Revolut Business and Wise Business. Legal constraints: EMIs may provide payment services and a disputed-float account, but they are not credit institutions and cannot offer a secured capital-escrow account over a corporate investment; they also cannot provide overdraft or other treasury lending facilities. The SAS must verify the EMI holds a valid ACPR or passported license (Regafi registry) and understand that funds held at an EMI are not covered by the French deposit guarantee (FGDR). Offshore EMIs outside the EEA are practically unsuitable because they lack French IBANs and PSD2 passporting rights, which would create FX controls, sanctions, and tax-reporting friction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law permits fully remote corporate onboarding through an authorized digital-KYC process (video identification, electronic signature, official corporate registry extraction [Kbis]) where the legal representative is an EEA resident. A physical visit to a branch is required only in exceptional cases, e.g., if a UBO is a politically exposed person (PEP), if the company's business model involves cash-intensive operations, or if the bank's own risk policy demands an in-person interview for a non-EEA resident director. For a low-risk online cosmetics retailer with a French-resident president, a completely paperless/remote opening is feasible at all major French banks, provided the SAS supplies a notarized/legalized ID for any non-EU UBO and a complete list of direct and indirect beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large proportionate gross turnover relative to declared e-commerce transaction values when using payment aggregators (Shopify Payments, PayPal), creating confusion between true sales and PSP settlement flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the signed PCI DSS compliance attestation, (ii) commercial platform agreements with Shopify and PayPal, (iii) a 12-month transaction forecast with split of gross and net settlement amounts, (iv) audited or management accounts showing revenue reconciliation to PSP log files, and (v) a written operational explanation of rolling reserves and chargeback procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows to/from non-EU markets, including beauty-supply imports from Asia, creating potential sanctions, customs, or tax-qualification questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an up-to-date matrix of active sales jurisdictions, customs import licences, EU/EC cosmetics compliance documents (Product Information File per Regulation EC No. 1223/2009), VAT and e-commerce-specific registrations (OSS/IOSS), and a confirmation letter from the bank's sanctions screening team that no shipment addresses are in restricted territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU beneficial ownership (UBO) held through a foreign holding structure, especially where the ultimate director is a remote individual without a French tax residence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a UBO declaration (under Article L.561-2-2 Monetary and Financial Code), certified passport copies, proof of residential address, an overseas tax file number, and a bank reference letter from the majority shareholder's own regulated financial institution. Additionally, provide legal documents demonstrating the source of capital contribution (e.g., approved shareholder resolution, notarized transfer agreement, or signed gift/sale contract).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funds expected to be received from international payment providers (PSPs) that are themselves unlicensed in France, or where the PSP's settlement account is located in a third country not recognized under EU equivalence rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce the PSP's FATF membership evidence, MIFID II/PSD2 registration, a copy of its French or host-country operating licence, confirmation that the PSP's settlement flows are routed through a French-licensed correspondent bank, and provide the bank with a technical integration diagram proving the PSP only acts as an intermediary and never takes legal title to the goods.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for an inbound shareholder loan or additional equity contribution: (i) send a SWIFT MT103 to the French company's bank, using the official IBAN and a detailed remittance field containing 'Capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan per statutes, notarized resolution dated [date]'; (ii) include the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment (commonly code 'C1' or 'D3' for capital transfers) in the message; (iii) transmit a copy of the SAS's Kbis certificate and an internal board/shareholder resolution authorizing the inflows and specifying the amount, currency, and final authorized capital; (iv) provide a source-of-funds letter for the sending bank; and (v) where the amount crosses the current statutory threshold for cross-border reporting, file the Banque de France direct-investment survey (RFE) within 30 calendar days. The sending party must ensure the deposit is made only after the bank has confirmed acceptance of the proposed account classification to avoid triggering anti-money-laundering review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For upstream supplier payments (cosmetic ingredients, packaging, finished goods), the standard clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for small and medium-value transfers (below EUR 250,000) with complete invoice references and commodity codes in field 70; (ii) Commercial Documentary Collections (URC 522) for medium-risk or new trading relationships; and (iii) an irrevocable Letter of Credit (ICC UCP 600) for high-value or first-time trade orders, especially with Asian manufacturers, ensuring the LC is opened at a tier-1 French bank with a corresponding-bank confirmation. All outgoing payments must include a customs declaration reference (for shipments involving global logistics), and the bank will require the supplier to have been KYC'd by a French correspondent bank; additionally, the SAS must ensure that no payment is made to entities subject to EU sanctions or countermeasures.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/GBP/USD) executed under an ISDA or French Master Agreement with a licensed French or EEA credit institution, provided the underlying commercial exposure is documented.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with no deliverability in the eurozone (e.g., KRW, CNY, INR) where the trade is supported by a real FX exposure and the counterparty is an ACPR-licensed bank or EEA financial institution.
FX Swaps (swap de change) to cover both principal and interest flows on multi-currency shareholder loans, with the transaction reported in the Banque de France balance-of-payments survey.

Currency Option Combinations (collars, risk reversals) through a licensed swap dealer, subject to MiFID II suitability and EMIR margin requirements, appropriate for hedging large forecast sales in volatile currencies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) and Management Report filing with the Commercial Court Greffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (via Infogreffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of Ordinary General Meeting approval; OGM must be held within 6 months of fiscal year-end (i.e., by 30 June for 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,500 per financial statement set; additional EUR 1,500 for management report. Continued non-filing triggers injunction, personal liability of directors, and potential judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration of Beneficial Owners (Déclaration des Beneficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS) - Greffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within 30 days of the anniversary of the initial registration; any change must be filed within 30 days.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 7,500 per infringing entity for failure to file or filing inaccurate information. Non-compliance may result in criminal liability for directors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Return (Liasse Fiscale) - Corporate Income Tax (IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 March for 31 December year-end). Extended deadlines apply for electronic filing based on turnover.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% (spontaneous) or 40% (formal notice) of additional tax due. Interest at 0.20% per month. Failure to file may trigger assessment of a minimum tax base.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value Added Tax (TVA) Summary Declaration (CA3) and Annual Recapitulative Statement (DAS2)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly CA3 filing; DAS2 due by 15 February of the year following the fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 0.40% per month plus 5% surcharge. Repeated non-compliance may result in suspension of VAT deduction rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises - CFE) Declaration and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration by 31 December of the previous year (initial filing) or 2nd working day after 15 December for existing entities; payment due by 15 December of the current year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% plus interest of 0.20% per month. Non-payment may lead to tax collection enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a Commissaire aux Comptes (statutory auditor) if at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at the end of the fiscal year: total assets > EUR 4,000,000; turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees > 50. For SAS, this is mandatory regardless of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan Comptable General - PCG) aligned with IFRS for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SAS must file an annual confirmation of beneficial owners with the RCS within 30 days of the anniversary of registration. Any change in beneficial ownership or control must be filed within 30 days. The declaration must identify natural persons holding >25% of capital or voting rights, or exercising control by other means.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 5% of eligible expenses), accelerated depreciation, SME reduced rate of 15% on first €42,500 of taxable income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 May following fiscal year-end (e.g. 15 May for FY ending 31 December)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 40% penalty on additional tax plus 0.5% daily surcharge after deadline

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC and DTA application documents to impots.gouv.fr for relief
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0-25% statutory and treaty rates; Interest: 0-10% statutory and treaty rates

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French ESR requires demonstration of economic substance for certain entities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understatement of profits or false tax declarations
